full_judgment:
3. The trial Court dismissed the suit after finding that the plaintiff was given an opportunity to show cause and defend himself. On appeal the appellate court, however, decreed the suit. It found that on 28 February 1988 the plaintiff was only asked to answer to four questions, and he submitted his answers. No witness was examined by the school authority. The enquiry committee started its proceeding with Mr. Nurullah, the Headmaster of the New Model High School, as the teacher representative. Later on, in place of Mr. Nurullah, Mr. Harun-ur-Rashid was included in the enquiry committee as the teacher representative. The plaintiff was asked to appear before the enquiry committee on 7 April 1988 at 3:00 PM. As on that date Mr. Harun-ur-Rashid was absent, the appellate Court held that the enquiry committee ought to have, in law and equity, adjourned its proceeding to another date, but the defendants without fixing another date for enquiry committee obtained an ex pane report from the enquiry committee and dismissed the plaintiff. According to the appellate Court, the plaintiff did not get full opportunity to defend himself and, that though there was no provision in the Regulations for second show cause notice before dismissal the plaintiff ought to have been given, in interest of justice, a second show cause notice. The High Court Division upheld the judgment of the court of appeal below. 

 5. Taking a cue from a query from this Court whether the order of approval by the Board was challenged in the suit, the learned Counsel for the appellant raised a new plea that the plaintiffs failure to challenge the order of approval of the Board by appropriately amending the plaint would make the decree made by the appellate Court as inconsequential. He has cited two cases. In Bauribandhu Misra Vs. IG of Police and others AIR 1970 Orissa 213 where a new point, not mentioned in the petition, was allowed to be raised when accuracy of factual basis of statement was not disputed. In RJ Singh Vs. State of Delhi AIR 1971 (SC) 1552 (1553) a jurisdictional point as to whether the sanction for the prosecution was granted by the Government was allowed to be raised for the first time in the Supreme Court. The new plea need not be considered if the order of dismissal is found to be in order. 

 13. The reasonings of the appellate Court are flawed. The High Court Division ought to have disapproved such judicial latitudinarianism. The plaintiff had the full opportunity to examine the papers and place his case. He did not ask for any personal hearing, nor did he ask for examination of any witness or production of any document. The enquiry report, on the basis of papers and the plaintiffs answer to the committee's queries, was endorsed by, all the three members. The order of dismissal, based on that report, was approved by the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education. At the trial the plaintiff did not challenge the order of dismissal or its approval by the Board in the manner it was assailed at the appellate stage. There is no merit in the plaintiffs cause. The appeal is allowed. The judgment and decree of the trial Court are restored and those of the appellate Court and the High Court Division are set aside. No costs.
